I1.evidence: The data are encoded as an OxCal chronological model, a formal, shared domain language. 'The revised chronological model was implemented in OxCal ... Caveat: the paper does not state the supplement's file format.

I2.evidence: Bead types follow a published typology ('bead identifications by an expert (Nielsen, 2013) according to an established classification (Brugmann, 2004)'), but that typology is not a FAIR vocabulary with PIDs or a machine-readable form. I3.evidence: The derivation relation to the upstream source is stated explicitly, with a typed PID citation: 'Chronological relations among the female graves are based on a chronological prior from the OxCal model deposited in the project archive (Hines, 2013)'. R1.evidence: The paper describes the model structure (two sections: likelihoods and constraints; bead-type occurrences), its scope (72 female graves, 23 bead types), the software version (OxCal 4.4.2), the calibration curve (IntCal20), and a stability check ('five independent runs of the model indicate negligible between-run variability'), p. 9-11.

R1_1.evidence: No licence is stated for the Supplement or its data, so it defaults to same-as-paper (R1.1 rule (a)). The article licence sources disagree. The White Rose accepted-version copy says CC-BY-NC-ND. The Crossref record for the publisher-hosted version of record (which serves the supplement) lists only Elsevier publisher terms (elsevier.com/tdm/userlicense/1.0, tdmrep-license, STM policy URIs). The most-restrictive rule makes the publisher's proprietary user/TDM terms govern. These are not an identified data-usage licence granting reuse, so R1.1 = 0. Judgement point: the CC notice attaches to the repository AAM copy, not the publisher-hosted supplement.

R1_2.evidence: Provenance is detailed. The model derives from the Hines (2013) ADS OxCal model, with three enumerated constraints removed: (i) a uniform-burial sequence, (ii) a bead-type sequence from Table 7.18, and (iii) a combined age determination for MaDE1/MaDE2 that fails an X^2 test (p. 10-11). The 20 Lakenheath graves were added from Hines (2021). Software version, calibration curve, and authorship of the supplementary material are given ('TSD drafted ... the supplementary material').

R1_3.evidence: The supplement-only deposit applies no deposit-level metadata standard (DataCite, Dublin Core, or a domain schema) and sits in no accredited domain repository. OxCal and IntCal20 are methodological standards and do not qualify (v2.1 R1.3 boundary).
